title: Police Salary: How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay in Australia
description: Learn how to convert an hourly rate to annual salary for police and other roles. Includes national minimum wage, award rates, tax, and super calculations.
salarySummary: For a police officer earning $40 per hour, the annual salary based on 38 hours per week is approximately $79,040 before tax and super.

faqs.q: What is the national minimum wage in Australia?
faqs.a: From 1 July 2026, the national minimum wage is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making it $33.05 per hour. This is the base rate for award/agreement-free employees.

Police salaries are set by state or territory enterprise agreements or awards, and vary by rank and years of service. They are generally higher than the national minimum wage. For specific rates, refer to the relevant award or agreement, or use the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay and Conditions Tool.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the national minimum wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The national minimum wage is the minimum pay for employees not covered by an award or agreement. Award rates are higher minimums set by the Fair Work Commission for specific industries, including police. From 1 July 2026, award wages increased by 4.75%.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Basics of Hourly to Annual Conversion

When you have an hourly rate, the simplest way to estimate your annual salary is to multiply that rate by the number of hours you work per week and then by 52 weeks. For full-time employees, the standard assumption is 38 hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Commission. The formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For example, at the national minimum wage of $26.44 per hour, the annual salary is $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.80 before tax and super. If you are paid a fortnightly salary, that is simply your weekly pay multiplied by two. For the minimum wage, the fortnightly gross is $2,009.80.

This calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. It is a starting point for comparing offers or budgeting.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The national minimum wage is the legal floor for award/agreement-free employees. From 1 July 2026, it is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for 38 ordinary hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top, making the casual rate $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for the lack of paid leave.

However, most employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates. For example, the Fair Work Ombudsman publishes pay guides for each award, and from 1 July 2026, award minimum wages increased by 4.75%. Police officers are typically covered by state-specific awards or enterprise agreements, which set rates well above the national minimum wage. According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 in May 2026, which equates to an annual salary of about $108,352.40. Police salaries often exceed this average, especially for senior ranks.

When evaluating a police salary offer, always check the applicable award or agreement rather than relying solely on the national minimum wage. The [pay guides](/blog) on the Fair Work Ombudsman website are a reliable source for award rates.

## Police Salary Considerations

The term "police salary" covers a range of pay points depending on rank, experience, and location. For instance, a constable in their first year may earn a different rate than a senior sergeant. The Australian Taxation Office provides a guide for police officers on income and work-related deductions, but it does not list specific salary figures. Instead, it outlines which allowances (e.g., shift penalties, overtime) must be included in your tax return and which expenses you can claim.

When converting an hourly police rate to annual pay, use the same formula: hourly rate × 38 hours × 52 weeks. However, police often work shift work and may receive penalty rates or allowances that increase their actual take-home pay. The simple conversion does not account for these extras. For a more accurate estimate, consider using the [the timesheet](/), which allows you to input your base hourly rate and add casual loading if applicable. Remember, casual loading is an additional 25% on top of the base rate, not included in the base rate itself.

## Tax and Superannuation

Once you have your annual gross salary, you need to estimate tax and super. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- Over $190,000: 45% on excess over $190,000

In addition, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The tax-free threshold is included. Note that the Medicare levy reduction thresholds used here are from 2025–26, as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this guide.

Superannuation is paid on top of your salary by your employer. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, on a $80,000 salary, the super contribution would be $9,600 per year. This is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional benefit.

To see your estimated take-home pay after tax and Medicare, visit the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page. For more on super and salary packaging, see [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [the timesheet](/) is designed to help you convert an hourly rate to annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures. Simply enter your base hourly rate. If you are a casual employee, check the box to add 25% casual loading. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading; the calculator will apply it for you.

The calculator uses the 38-hour week assumption and the 2026–27 tax scale. It provides an estimate only, as it does not account for HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. Always consult a tax professional for your specific situation.

## Conclusion

Understanding how to convert an hourly rate to an annual salary is essential for comparing job offers, budgeting, and planning. Whether you are looking at a police salary or any other role, the formula remains the same: hourly × hours per week × 52. Remember to distinguish between the national minimum wage, award rates, and casual loading. Use reliable sources like the Fair Work Commission and the Fair Work Ombudsman for official rates, and the Australian Taxation Office for tax guidance. Our [reference tables](/data) provide additional data on average earnings and tax brackets.

For further reading, check out [average pay](/topics/average-pay) to see how your salary compares nationally, or [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) for more examples. If you are a casual worker, the [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) page explains how the 25% loading works. And for industry-specific pay, including police, the [job pay](/topics/job-pay) page offers insights.
